newsitem.title: USA: NHL, AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DEVILS PLACE NEAL BROTEN ON WAIVERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL, AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DEVILS PLACE NEAL BROTEN ON WAIVERS.

text.p: Veteran centre Neal Broten, the last active member of the miracle 1980 U.S. Olympic gold medal hockey team, fell victim to the New Jersey Devils youth movement on Tuesday.
Broten, who had one assist in the Devils' first three games, was placed on waivers by General Manager Lou Lamoriello, who said the 37-year-old centre no longer fit into the team's plans.
"The decision was made to go with a couple of younger players at that position," Lamoriello told the New York Daily News.
"This is where you have to separate your feelings and your head," Lamoriello said. "This is a player who has given a lot to the game. It's difficult, but these are things you have to do."
The Devils acquired Broten from Dallas in February 1995 and he became a key member of New Jersey's Stanley Cup championship team that year.
Broten scored the Cup-winning goal in the Devils' stunning four-game sweep of the Detroit Red Wings in the lockout-shortened 1995 season.
Broten has 281 goals and 623 assists in 1,060 career NHL games.

He is one of only two Americans to win an Olympic gold medal and the Stanley Cup. The other was Broten's 1980 Lake Placid teammate Ken Morrow, who collected four Stanley Cup rings with the New York Islanders in the early 1980s.
If no other team claims Broten within 48 hours, Lamoriello said he would assign him to a minor-league team.
